mmaths-2020-tiebreaker-01.title: Solution
mmaths-2020-tiebreaker-01.body:
Let $s(m)$ be the sum of the proper divisors of $m$; $n$ is untouchable iff no $m$ has $s(m)=n$. We find $s(2)=1$, $s(4)=3$, $s(9)=4$, $s(6)=6$, $s(8)=7$, $s(49)=8$, $s(15)=9$, $s(14)=10$. So only $2$ and $5$ remain.

- $2$: if $m$ is prime, $s(m)=1$; if $m=p^e$ with $e>1$, $s(m)\ge p+1\ge3$; if $m$ has two distinct prime factors $p,q$, $s(m)\ge1+p+q>2$. So $2$ is untouchable.
- $5$: primes give $1$ and numbers with two distinct primes give $s(m)\ge 1+p+q+\dots$; for $m=p^e$, $p\ge5$ gives $s>5$, while the powers of $2$ give $s=1,3,7,\dots$ and of $3$ give $s=1,4,13,\dots$, skipping $5$. For $m=pq$ with $p<q$ we get $s=1+p+q=5$ only if $p+q=4$, impossible for distinct primes; larger $m$ give larger $s$. So $5$ is untouchable.

The sum is $2+5=7$.

**Answer: 7**

mmaths-2020-tiebreaker-02.title: Solution
mmaths-2020-tiebreaker-02.body:
Since $C$ and $D$ trisect the arc, arcs $AD$, $DC$, $CB$ are equal, so $BC=CD=8$ and $\angle BDC=\angle CBD$. By the tangent-chord angle, $\angle BCE=\angle BDC=\angle CBD$, hence $DB\parallel CE$. Also arcs $AD$ and $CB$ are equal, so $DC\parallel AB$, i.e. $DC\parallel BE$. Hence $DCEB$ is a parallelogram with sides $DC=8$, $DB=11$ and diagonals $DE$ and $CB=8$. The parallelogram law gives $2(DC^2+DB^2)=DE^2+CB^2$, i.e. $2(64+121)=DE^2+64$, so $DE^2=306=9\cdot34$ and $DE=3\sqrt{34}$. Then $a+b=3+34=37$. (A coordinate check with the circle gives $DE\approx17.4929=3\sqrt{34}$.)

**Answer: 37**
